text:
Maya Patel: Alerting — rack-r5a-07 has 6 GPU nodes flapping, sudden PCIe resets and OOMs on inference pods. Prometheus shows token-gen latency spike 3x.
Kai Chen: Seen alerts. Any kernel oops / dmesg snippets? Sounds like controller-level resets rather than NV driver OOM.
Maya Patel: Paste of dmesg from node-r5a-07-12:
```
[ 1234.567890] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: pciehp: Slot #23 Link Down
[ 1234.568120] nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[ 1234.570001] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid 2245, GPU 0: nvlink timeout
[ 1234.570010] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2245 (inference) total-vm:233M
```
Maya Patel: Happens across multiple nodes in that rack within a minute.
Liam O'Neill: I'm cordoning + draining the affected nodes now. Command I'm running: `kubectl drain node-r5a-07-{10..15} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
infra-bot: Cluster update: 6 nodes cordoned; eviction started (eviction controller). Pod disruption budgets respected.
Sasha Rivera: Routing plan — shifting inference traffic off eu-west-3->primary pool to eu-west-2 warm pool. Enabling fallback-route policy for rps-heavy routes. Will toggle at 80% CPU.
Kai Chen: Can autoscaler grab extra Dedicated GPUs or do we need to spin up hosted instances? What's the failover cost if we keep fallback for 24h?
Noah Brooks: Quick cost calc: spinning 8 p4d-like GPUs in hosted bursts ~ $1.9k/day, pushing to dedicated reserved pools would be ~ $1.3k/day but needs procurement. For 48h expect ~ $3.8k hosted. Approve?
Sasha Rivera: Approved from infra side — do hosted burst for now, keep customers on SLAs. Notify support.
Liam O'Neill: Vendor contacted — ticket #GALX-8942 opened, flagged as "controller board intermittent PCIe resets". RMA requested for rack-r5a-07 controller backplane. ETA 48h for replacement parts.
Kai Chen: Plan for nodes: keep drained, disable autoscaler scaling-up into those racks, rebuild firmware on a spare node with test image `fwtest-2026-03-15` and run 6h burn-in. If stable, we can image others.
Maya Patel: Customer impact — Support reported 2 customers with elevated 95th latency and one failed job; most traffic rerouted. Creating incident ticket INC-20260315-42 and will update status page.
oncall-bot: Alert cleared for node-r5a-07-13 at 1712345820 (health checks recovered after pod relocation).
Kai Chen: After parts in -> we'll do canary firmware roll: 2 racks at a time, 4 nodes per rack. Add a canary test running quantized-8bit model workload for perf regressions.
Maya Patel: I'll update the infra runbook with mitigation steps, add the RMA and rollback checklist, and start a postmortem draft.
Liam O'Neill: Leaving notes in the ticket with drain commands used and which pods were evicted. Will coordinate swap window with vendor when arrival ETA firmed.
Sasha Rivera: TL;DR — drained affected nodes, traffic shifted to warm pool, vendor RMA in flight, running burst GPUs to cover capacity, cost approved short-term. Monitoring closely. :eyes:
Maya Patel: Thanks all — will keep this thread updated as we get firmware/parts ETA.
